Short summary: the claim does not hold as stated — the cited evidence (peak read-QPS, next-tier instance cost) cannot establish that the real bottleneck is read-bound rather than write/vacuum/lock-bound, cannot establish the cache's achievable hit rate, and cannot establish that "reduces average load" and "cuts p95 enough" are the same thing. Recommendation (HIGH confidence): don't bet the expensively-reversible side of the decision on it — execute the scheduled upgrade now, ship the cache in parallel on a correctness-scoped build (invalidation + anti-stampede, not just GET/SET), and name a checkpoint owner and date before the next capacity cycle to decide, on measured data, whether a future upgrade can be skipped.
